summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and migraines was admitted for abdominal pain, headache, nausea, vomiting, and chest pressure. She had elevated blood pressure and blood glucose on presentation. Evaluation ruled out acute cardiac ischemia with normal ECGs and negative troponins. A CT scan revealed significant fecal loading, explaining her abdominal symptoms. Her headache, consistent with her migraine history, improved with acetaminophen and blood pressure control. Hyponatremia was corrected with IV fluids. Constipation was treated with senna, bisacodyl, and continued docusate, leading to bowel movements overnight. Her Lantus insulin dose was increased to 50 units due to persistent hyperglycemia. She engaged with social work regarding unsafe housing conditions. She was discharged home in stable condition with medication adjustments and follow-up plans.
